summary: 超市借货架位置、商品选择和顾客行为数据影响购买。文章一边展示这些技术，一边追问它们的实际效果和隐蔽劝购的界线。
logic: 超市布局、气味与停留时间
情绪与潜意识如何参与购买决定
货架陈列与顾客选择的瞬间
选项过多如何妨碍购买
电子标签与个性化推销
隐性说服的反弹与结账现场的限制

paragraphs.brief: 超市布局背后的购物心理学
sentences: It may have occurred to you, during the course of a dismal trawl round a supermarket indistinguishable from every other supermarket you have ever been into, to wonder why they are all the same.
推着车在一家与其他超市如出一辙的店里闷闷地逛时，你也许想过，为什么超市都一个样？
The answer is more sinister than depressing.
答案与其说令人扫兴，不如说让人不安。
It is not because the companies that operate them lack imagination.
并不是因为经营这些企业的公司缺乏想象力。

It is because they are all versed in the science of persuading people to buy things—a science that, thanks to technological advances, is beginning to unlock the innermost secrets of the consumer’s mind.
因为他们都精通说服人们买东西的科学，这种科学由于技术进步而开始解开消费者思想中最隐秘的秘密。
paragraphs.gist: 超市面貌相似是因为经营者都熟悉劝人购买的办法，而不断进步的技术正帮助他们了解消费者自己都未必察觉的心理。

paragraphs.brief: 入口减压区与迎宾服务
sentences: In the Sainsbury’s in Hatch Warren, Basingstoke, south-west of London, it takes a while for the mind to get into a shopping mode.
走进伦敦西南、贝辛斯托克哈奇沃伦的森宝利超市，人得花一会儿才能进入购物状态。
This is why the area immediately inside the entrance of a supermarket is known as the “decompression zone”.
因此，超市入口处附近地区被称为“减压区”。
People need to slow down and take stock of the surroundings, even if they are regulars.
人们需要减速，评估周围环境，即使他们是常客。
In sales terms, this area is a bit of a loss, so it tends to be used more for promotion.
就销售而言，入口这片区域贡献不大，所以更多用来做推广。
Even the multi-packs of beer piled up here are designed more to hint at bargains within than to be lugged round the aisles.
连这里堆放的整组啤酒，也是为了暗示店里还有便宜货，而非真指望人提着它逛遍过道。
Wal-Mart, the world’s biggest retailer, famously employs “greeters” at the entrance to its stores.
世界最大的零售商沃尔玛就以在店门口专设迎宾员闻名。
Whether or not they boost sales, a friendly welcome is said to cut shoplifting.
不论迎宾员能否提高销量，据说亲切的问候能减少店内行窃。
It is harder to steal from nice people.
偷好人的东西很难
paragraphs.gist: 刚进门的人需要放慢脚步、适应环境，因此超市多用入口暗示店内优惠；沃尔玛还安排迎宾员，据说亲切的招呼能减少行窃。

paragraphs.brief: 休闲浏览区先于果蔬区
sentences: Immediately to the left in Sainsbury’s is another familiar sight: a “chill zone” for browsing magazines, books and DVDs, tempting impromptu purchases and slowing customers down.
在这家森宝利超市里，紧靠左手边又是一处常见场景：顾客可以在“休闲区”翻阅杂志、书籍和 DVD。这既让他们放慢脚步，也容易诱发即兴购买。
But those on a serious mission will keep walking ahead—and the first thing they come to is the fresh fruit and vegetables section.
不过，目的明确的顾客会径直向前，首先遇到新鲜果蔬区。
paragraphs.gist: 入口旁的休闲区用书刊和影碟留住随意浏览的顾客，目标明确、继续向前走的人则会先遇到生鲜果蔬区。

paragraphs.brief: 先买健康食品的心理作用
sentences: For shoppers, this makes no sense.
对顾客来说，这说不通
Fruit and vegetables can be easily damaged, so they should be bought at the end, not the beginning, of a shopping trip.
水果和蔬菜很容易损坏，因此应在购物之旅的最后而不是开始时购买。
But psychology is at work here: selecting good wholesome fresh food is an uplifting way to start shopping, and it makes people feel less guilty about reaching for the stodgy stuff later on.
这里利用了购物心理：先挑健康新鲜的食物能让人心情愉快，稍后再拿厚重顶饱的食品时也就少些内疚。
paragraphs.gist: 易压坏的果蔬照理应最后买，超市却让顾客先挑健康食品，因为这能让人心情愉快，稍后再买厚重高热量的食物时也少些内疚。

paragraphs.brief: 用商品位置延长留店时间
sentences: Shoppers already know that everyday items, like milk, are invariably placed towards the back of a store to provide more opportunity to tempt customers.
顾客早已知道，牛奶之类日常必需品往往放在店铺深处，让商家有更多机会用沿途商品吸引他们。
This is why pharmacies are generally at the rear, even in “convenience” stores.
这就是为什么药店一般在后方，甚至在“便利”店里。
But supermarkets know shoppers know this, so they use other tricks, like placing popular items halfway along a section so that people have to walk all along the aisle looking for them.
超市也知道顾客明白这一招，还会用其他办法，例如把热销品放在一排货架的中段，让人沿通道一路寻找。
The idea is to boost “dwell time”: the length of time people spend in a store.
目的是延长「停留时间」，也就是顾客在店里待多久。
paragraphs.gist: 牛奶、药房常放在深处，畅销品有时又藏在一排货架中段，让顾客为找东西走得更远，延长留店时间并多接触商品。

paragraphs.brief: 手机定位揭示停留与销售的关系
sentences: Traditionally retailers measure “footfall”, as the number of people entering a store is known, but those numbers say nothing about where people go and how long they spend there.
零售商过去通常只统计「客流量」，即进店人数；这个数字却看不出顾客去了哪里、停了多久。
But nowadays, a ubiquitous piece of technology can fill the gap: the mobile phone.
但如今，无处不在的技术可以填补空白：移动电话。

Path Intelligence, a British company working with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, tracked people’s phones at Gunwharf Quays, a large retail and leisure centre in Portsmouth—not by monitoring calls, but by plotting the positions of handsets as they transmit automatically to cellular networks.
与麻省理工学院合作的英国公司 Path Intelligence 在朴次茅斯的大型购物休闲中心 Gunwharf Quays 追踪手机位置：它并不监听通话，而是根据手机自动与移动网络联络时的信号绘出位置。
It found that when dwell time rose 1%, sales rose 1.3%.
公司发现，顾客停留时间每增加1%，销售额就增加1.3%。
paragraphs.gist: 传统客流量看不出顾客去向，研究者用手机与基站的信号描绘动线，发现该购物中心停留时间每增加 1%，销售额便增加 1.3%。

paragraphs.brief: 店内面包香如何带动其他购买
sentences: Having walked to the end of the fruit and vegetable aisle, Basingstoke’s hard-core shoppers arrive at counters of prepared food, the fishmonger, the butcher and the deli.
一路往前的顾客走到果蔬区尽头后，会看到预制食品、鲜鱼、肉类和熟食柜台。
Then there is the in-store bakery, which can be smelt before it is seen.
再往前是店内烘焙坊，往往还没看见就先闻到香味。
Even small supermarkets now use in-store bakeries.
连小超市现在都用店内面包店
Mostly these bake pre-prepared items and frozen dough, and they have boomed even though central bakeries that deliver to a number of stores are much more efficient.
店内烘焙多半只需烤制预制品与冷冻面团；尽管由中央烘焙坊统一配送给多家店效率更高，店内烘焙却越来越兴旺。
They do it for the smell of freshly baked bread, which makes people hungry and thus encourages people to buy not just bread but also other food, including frozen stuff.
商家图的是新烤面包的香味，它让人感到饿，从而多买的不只是面包，还有冷冻食品等其他食物。
paragraphs.gist: 店内烘焙不如集中生产高效，超市仍愿意烤制预制面团，因为新出炉的面包香会勾起食欲，连其他食品都更容易卖出去。

paragraphs.brief: 香味与声音辅助卖场营销
sentences: Most of the information that shoppers are bombarded with is visual: labels, price stickers and advertising.
购物者受到轰炸的大部分信息是视觉的：标签、贴纸和广告。
But the wafting bread aroma shows smell can usefully be stimulated too, says Simon Harrop, chief executive of Brand Sense Agency, a British specialist in multi-sensory marketing.
英国多感官营销机构 Brand Sense Agency 的负责人西蒙·哈罗普说，但飘来的面包香表明，商家也可以有效调动嗅觉。
In the aisle by the laundry section, he suggests introducing the smell of freshly laundered sheets.
他建议在洗衣用品区旁的过道引入刚洗过的床单的清香。
Even the sound of sheets being folded could be reproduced here and contained within the area using the latest audio technology.
甚至可以重现折叠床单的声音，再用最新音响技术让声音只在这个区域内传播。
The Aroma Company, which Mr Harrop founded, has put the smell of coconut into the shops of Thomson, a British travel agent.
Harrop先生创建的Aroma公司，在英国旅行社Thomson的商店里散发了椰子味。
Some suntan oils smell of coconut, so the scent is supposed to remind people of past holidays.
有些防晒油带有椰香，因此这种气味被用来勾起人们对以往假期的回忆。
The company even infuses the fresh smell of citrus into a range of clothing made by Odeur, a Swedish company.
该公司甚至将柑橘的新鲜味道注入瑞典公司Odeur制造的一系列衣服中。
It can waft for up to 13 washes.
衣服洗过多达十三次，仍能散发香味。
paragraphs.gist: 多感官营销把香味和声音带入以视觉为主的卖场，例如用椰香使旅行社顾客想起假期，或让衣物的柑橘香保持多次洗涤。

paragraphs.brief: 购买理由与潜意识影响
sentences: Such techniques are increasingly popular because of a deepening understanding about how shoppers make choices.
这种技术越来越受欢迎，因为人们越来越了解顾客如何作出选择。
People tell market researchers and “focus groups” that they make rational decisions about what to buy, considering things like price, selection or convenience.
顾客告诉市场研究者，也在焦点小组访谈中说，他们会权衡价格、选择范围和便利性，理性决定买什么。
But subconscious forces, involving emotion and memories, are clearly also at work.
但潜意识的力量，包括情感和记忆，也显然在起作用。
paragraphs.gist: 顾客常说自己依据价格、选择和便利性理性购物，但情绪与记忆也会暗中影响决定，这正是感官营销日益受欢迎的原因。

paragraphs.brief: 情绪对作出决定的重要性
sentences: Scientists used to assume that emotion and rationality were opposed to each other, but Antonio Damasio, now professor of neuroscience at the University of Southern California, has found that people who lose the ability to perceive or experience emotions as the result of a brain injury find it hard or impossible to make any decisions at all.
科学家过去认为情绪和理性是相互对立的，但是现在的南加州大学神经科学教授 Antonio Damasio发现，由于脑损伤而失去感知或体验情绪能力的人很难或根本无法做出任何决定。
They can’t shop.
他们不能购物。
paragraphs.gist: 达马西奥发现，脑损伤后难以感受情绪的人连一般决定都很难做，购物也成了难事，说明情绪与理性决策并非相互排斥。

paragraphs.brief: 用脑成像对照口头购买意愿
sentences: Researchers are now exploring these mechanisms by observing the brain at work.
研究人员正在通过观察大脑的工作来探索这些机制。

One of the most promising techniques is functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), which uses a large scanner to detect changes in the blood flow in parts of the brain that correspond to increases or decreases in mental activity.
很有前景的一项技术是功能磁共振成像，它用大型扫描仪检测局部脑血流的变化，借此判断精神活动增强还是减弱。
People lying inside the scanners are shown different products or brands and then asked questions about them.
受试者躺在扫描仪里观看不同商品或品牌，再回答相关问题。
What they say is compared with what they are thinking by looking at cognitive or emotional activity.
研究者观察与认知或情感有关的脑活动，把受试者说的话和他们可能的真实想法加以比较。
The idea is that if, say, a part of the brain that is associated with pleasure lights up, then the product could be a winner.
其设想是，如果与愉悦有关的脑区变得活跃，这件商品就可能受到欢迎。

This is immensely valuable information because eight out of ten new consumer products usually fail, despite test marketing on people who say they would buy the item—but whose subconscious may have been thinking something different.
这种信息非常宝贵：十种新消费品通常有八种会失败，尽管参与市场测试的人表示会买，他们的潜意识想法可能并不相同。
paragraphs.gist: 研究者用功能磁共振观察受试者看商品时的脑区活动，再与口头回答对照，希望找出消费者表示想买却最终不买的线索。

paragraphs.brief: 商业保密限制对研究结果的了解
sentences: “We are just at the frontier of the subconscious,” says Eric Spangenberg, dean of the College of Business at Washington State University and an expert on the subtleties of marketing.
华盛顿州立大学商学院院长、研究细微营销手法的专家埃里克·斯潘根伯格说：「我们才刚摸到潜意识的边缘。」
“We know it’s there, we know there are responses and we know it is significant.”
“我们知道它在那里，我们知道有反应，我们知道它很重要。”
But companies commissioning such studies keep the results secret for commercial reasons.
但是，出于商业原因，委托进行这种研究的公司对研究结果保密。
This makes Dr Spangenberg sure of one thing: “What I think I know, they probably know way more.”
这让斯潘根贝格博士确信一件事：“我想我知道的，他们可能知道的更多。”
paragraphs.gist: 研究者已能观察到潜意识反应，也知道它们值得重视，但委托研究的企业通常保密，外界难以掌握商业应用的全貌。

paragraphs.role: 我们只是处在潜意识的边缘
paragraphs.brief: 货架高度影响伸手选择
sentences: Retailers and producers talk a lot about the “moment of truth”.
零售商和生产商常常谈到「决定性的一刻」。
This is not a philosophical notion, but the point when people standing in the aisle decide what to buy and reach to get it.
这并非哲学概念，而是顾客站在通道里决定买什么并伸手去拿的那一刻。
The Basingstoke store illustrates some of the ways used to get shoppers’ hands to wobble in the direction of a particular product.
贝辛斯托克这家店就展示了怎样让顾客伸出去的手偏向某种特定商品。
At the instant coffee selection, for example, branded products from the big producers are arranged at eye-level while cheaper ones are lower down, along with the supermarket’s own-label products.
例如在速溶咖啡区，大厂的品牌咖啡放在视线高度，而便宜货和超市自有品牌放得较低。
sectionTitle: We are just at the frontier of the subconscious
我们才刚开始探索潜意识
paragraphs.gist: 顾客站在货架前伸手的那一刻是商家眼中的关键，例如把知名品牌速溶咖啡放在视线高度，把低价和自有品牌放低。

paragraphs.brief: 陈列图、上架费与抽查
sentences: Often head offices will send out elaborate plans of where everything has to be placed; Albertsons, a big American supermarket chain, calls these a “plan-o-gram”.
总部常下发详细图纸，规定各种商品应放在哪里；美国大型连锁超市 Albertsons 称之为「货架陈列图」。
Spot-checks are carried out to make sure instructions are followed to the letter.
公司还会抽查，确保各店一丝不差地照图执行。
The reason for this strictness is that big retailers demand “slotting fees” to put suppliers’ goods on their shelves, and these vary according to which positions are considered to be prime space.
之所以如此严格，是因为大零售商会向供应商收取上架费，而被视为黄金货位的位置收费更高。
paragraphs.gist: 总部为各店制作细致的货架陈列图，还会抽查执行情况，因为供应商为不同位置支付的上架费与位置价值紧密相关。

paragraphs.brief: 货架黄金位置之争
sentences: But shelf-positioning is fiercely fought over, not just by those trying to sell goods, but also by those arguing over how best to manipulate shoppers.
围绕货架位置的争夺十分激烈，不仅卖家想抢好位置，研究如何引导顾客的人对怎样摆放最好也争论不休。
Never mind all the academic papers written on how best to stack shelves, retailers have their own views.
尽管学术界写了许多论文研究怎样陈列货架最有效，零售商自己也有一套看法。
While many stores reckon eye-level is the top spot, some think a little higher is better.
虽然很多商店认为眼睛水平是顶尖的，但有些人认为再高一点更好。

Others charge more for goods placed on “end caps”—displays at the end of the aisles, which they reckon to have the greatest visibility (although some experts say it all depends on the direction in which people gyrate around a store—and opinion on that is also divided).
有些商家对通道端头的陈列位收费更高，认为那里最醒目；也有专家认为还要看顾客在店里的行走方向，而这一点本身也有分歧。
To be on the right-hand side of an eye-level selection is often considered the very best place, because most people are right-handed and most people’s eyes drift rightwards.
与眼睛齐平且偏右的位置常被视为最佳，因为多数人惯用右手，视线也容易向右移。
Some supermarkets reserve that for their own-label “premium” goods.
有些超市把这个位置留给自己的高端品牌产品。
And supermarkets may categorise things in different ways, so chapatis may not be with breads, but with ready-meals of the Indian variety.
各家超市的分类也可能不同，例如印度薄饼未必放在面包区，而可能归入印度即食餐。
So, even though some suppliers could be paying around $50,000 per store a year for a few feet of shelf space, many customers still can’t find what they are looking for.
因此，即使有些供应商为了每家门店几英尺的货位一年付约五万美元，不少顾客还是找不到想买的东西。
paragraphs.gist: 视线高度、通道端头或偏右的位置各有支持者，分类规则也因店而异；即使供应商为货位付出高价，顾客仍可能找不到商品。

paragraphs.brief: 图像识别分析选购行为
sentences: Technology is making the process of monitoring shopper behaviour easier—which is why the security cameras in a store may be doing a lot more than simply watching out for theft.
技术使观察顾客的购物行为变得更容易，因此商店里的监控摄像头除了防盗，还可能有许多其他用途。
Rajeev Sharma, of Pennsylvania State University, founded a company called VideoMining to automate the process.
宾夕法尼亚州立大学的Rajeev Sharma 创建了一家名为VideoMining的公司，使这一过程自动化。
It uses image-recognition software to scan the pictures from security cameras of shoppers while they are making their selections.
该公司以图像识别软件分析顾客挑选商品时监控摄像头拍到的画面。
It is capable of looking at the actions of hundreds of thousands of people.
它可以分析数十万人的动作。
It can measure how many went straight to one brand, the number that dithered and those that compared several, at the same time as sorting shoppers by age, gender and ethnicity.
它能统计多少人直奔某品牌、多少人犹豫、多少人比较多个品牌，同时按年龄、性别和族裔对顾客进行分类。
paragraphs.gist: VideoMining 用图像识别分析监控画面，既能区分直奔某品牌、犹豫或比较的顾客，也能同时按年龄、性别等估计特征分组。

paragraphs.brief: 啤酒买家与果汁买家的差异
sentences: VideoMining analysed people in convenience stores buying beer.
VideoMining 分析了人们在便利店买啤酒的行为。
Typically, it would take them two minutes, with the majority going straight to one brand.
他们通常只花两分钟，大多数人直奔某个品牌。
“This shows their mind was already made up; they were on autopilot,” says Dr Sharma.
夏尔玛博士说：「这表明他们早已打定主意，只是在按习惯行动。」
So brewers should spend their marketing money outside, not inside, the store.
所以酿酒者应该花他们的营销钱在外面，而不是在店里。
The analysis can also help establish the return on investment to a new advertising campaign by showing what proportion of beer-buyers can be persuaded to consider rival brands.
分析还有助于确定投资对新广告运动的回报，显示可以说服多少比例的啤酒买家考虑竞争品牌。
In another study in a supermarket, some 12% of people spent 90 seconds looking at juices, studying the labels but not selecting any.
在另一所超市的研究中，大约12%的人花了90秒的时间寻找果汁，研究标签，但没有选择任何。
In supermarket decision-making time, that is forever.
按超市购物决策的时间尺度看，九十秒已经很久了。
This implies that shoppers are very interested in juices as a healthy alternative to carbonated drinks, but are not sure which to buy.
这意味着，买家非常关心果汁作为碳酸饮料的一种健康替代品，但不确定买什么。
So there is a lot of scope for persuasion.
所以说有很多说服的余地。
paragraphs.gist: 啤酒买家多半直接认准品牌，宜在进店前打广告；一些果汁买家却读了很久标签仍不下手，说明现场引导还有空间。

paragraphs.brief: 即使简单分类也能提高满意度
sentences: Reducing the selection on offer might help too.
减少供选择的商品数量也可能有帮助。
Cassie Mogilner of Stanford University and her colleagues found in a study that consumers like unfamiliar products to be categorised— even if the categories are meaningless.
斯坦福大学的Cassie Mogilner和她的同事在一项研究中发现，消费者喜欢不熟悉的产品被分类，即使分类毫无意义。

In a study of different coffees they found people were more satisfied with their choice if it came from a categorised selection, although it did not matter if the categories were marked simply A, B and C, or “mild”, “dark roast” and “nutty”.
咖啡实验发现，从分过类的商品中选择会使顾客更满意；分类是只标 A、B、C，还是写「温和」「深焙」「坚果风味」，并没有区别。
paragraphs.gist: 咖啡实验表明，顾客挑选不熟悉的商品时喜欢看到分类，即便标签只是没有实际含义的 A、B、C，选定后也更满意。

paragraphs.brief: 询问顾客了解成交转化率
sentences: Despite all the new technology, simply talking to consumers remains one of the most effective ways to improve the “customer experience”.
尽管有各种新技术，但仅仅与消费者交谈仍然是改进“客户经验”的最有效方法之一。
Scott Bearse, a retail expert with Deloitte Consulting in Boston, Massachusetts, has led projects observing and quizzing tens of thousands of customers about how they feel about shopping.
Scott Bearse是马萨诸塞州波士顿德勤咨询公司的零售专家，领导一些项目观察和测验成千上万的顾客，了解他们对购物的感受。

It began when a client complained that he had mountains of data on the one in four people that entered his store and bought something, but knew hardly anything about the vast majority who left without making a purchase.
项目源于一位客户的抱怨：进店的人中只有四分之一买了东西，他有大量关于这些买家的数据，却几乎不了解多数空手离店的人。
The “customer conversion” rate varies between types of store: it could be around 20% in some department stores but reach almost 100% in a grocery.
进店后实际购物的顾客比例因门店类型而异：有些百货商店约为 20%，而杂货店则接近 100%。
And within the same store the conversion rate will vary in different sections.
即便在同一家店，不同区域的成交转化率也会不同。
paragraphs.gist: 直接询问顾客有助于了解空手离开的原因，因为成交转化率不仅随商店类型大幅变化，同一家店的不同区域也各不相同。

paragraphs.brief: 犹豫、试穿与最终购买
sentences: People say they leave shops empty-handed more often because they are “unable to decide” than because prices are too high, says Mr Bearse.
贝瑟先生说的：“人们常说他们空手离开商店，因为他们“无法决定”，而不是价格太高。”
Working out what turns customers off is not difficult, yet stores still struggle with these issues: goods out of stock, long queues at the checkouts and poor levels of service.
弄清顾客为什么失去兴趣并不难，可店家依然受缺货、结账队伍过长和服务不佳等问题困扰。
Getting customers to try something is one of the best ways of getting them to buy, adds Mr Bearse.
贝尔斯补充说，让顾客实际试用商品是促进购买的最好方法之一。
Deloitte found that customers using fitting rooms convert at a rate of 85% compared with 58% for those that do not do so.
德勤发现，使用过试衣间的顾客中有85%最终购买，没试穿的顾客中则为58%。
paragraphs.gist: 犹豫不决比嫌贵更常成为空手离开的理由；调查还发现，使用试衣间的顾客有 85% 成交，未试穿者则为 58%。

paragraphs.brief: 第三件诱饵商品帮助二选一
sentences: Often a customer struggling to decide which of two items is best ends up not buying either.
顾客在两件商品之间难以判断哪件更好时，往往两件都不买。

A third “decoy” item, which is not quite as good as the other two, can make the choice easier and more pleasurable, according to a new study using fMRI carried out by Akshay Rao, a professor of marketing at the University of Minnesota.
根据明尼苏达大学销售教授Akshay Rao利用FMRI进行的一项新研究，第三个“诱饵”项目，它不如其他两个项目那么好，可以使选择更加容易，更令人愉快。
Happier customers are more likely to buy.
快乐的顾客更可能买。
Dr Rao believes the deliberate use of irrelevant alternatives should work in selling all sorts of goods and services, from cable TV to holidays.
拉奥博士认为，有意加入无关的备选项，应能帮助推销从有线电视服务到度假产品的各类商品与服务。
paragraphs.gist: 消费者在两件商品间拿不定主意时可能干脆不买，加入一件略逊色的「诱饵」能使比较更轻松，从而提高购买意愿。

paragraphs.role: 买家戴脑部扫描帽子的想法太荒谬了
paragraphs.brief: 射频标签与自动结账
sentences: A lack of price tags is another turn-off, although getting that right will become crucial with the increasing use of radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags.
没有价格标签也会使顾客打退堂鼓；随着射频识别标签越来越普遍，把标价这件事做好将十分关键。
These contain far more information than bar codes and can be scanned remotely.
这类标签比条形码容纳的信息多得多，还能远距离扫描。
People have been predicting for years that they would shortly become ubiquitous; but, with costs continuing to fall, they eventually will.
多年来人们一直预测射频标签很快会无所不在；随着成本继续下降，它们终将普及。
Tills will then become redundant, because everything shoppers put in their trolleys will be automatically detected and charged to their credit cards.
到那时连收银台都可能不再需要，因为顾客放进购物车的东西都会被自动识别，并从信用卡扣款。
sectionTitle: The notion of shoppers wearing brain-scanning hats would be ridiculous
让顾客戴着脑扫描帽购物，听起来很荒唐
paragraphs.gist: 射频识别标签比条形码能储存更多信息，还能远距离读取；作者预想成本降低后，购物车里的商品有望自动识别并扣款。

paragraphs.brief: 购物车按消费记录发出提醒
sentences: The basic mechanisms to do this are already in place.
已经建立了这方面的基本机制。
A store or loyalty card can be fitted with an RFID tag to identify customers on arrival.
商店会员卡或积分卡可以嵌入射频标签，在顾客到店时认出其身份。
A device on the trolley could monitor everything placed in it, check with past spending patterns and nudge customers: “You have just passed the Oreos, which you usually buy here.”
购物车上的设备可以记录放入的每件商品，对照以往消费习惯提醒顾客：「你刚走过平时在这儿常买的奥利奥饼干。」
paragraphs.gist: 带射频标签的会员卡可在入店时识别顾客，购物车还可根据历史消费提醒对方，刚才经过了平常喜欢买的奥利奥。

paragraphs.brief: 识别表情与头戴式脑电设备
sentences: Technology will also begin to identify customers’ emotions.
科技也将开始识别顾客的情绪。
Dr Sharma’s software has the potential to analyse expressions, like smiles and grimaces, which are hard to fake.
夏尔玛博士的软件有望分析微笑、做鬼脸等难以伪装的表情。
And although fMRI scanners presently need a crane to move, something that provides a similar result might one day be worn on your head.
尽管如今移动功能磁共振扫描仪还得用吊车，将来能提供类似结果的装置也许就能戴在头上。

Researchers believe it is possible to correlate brain patterns with changes in electrical activity in the brain, which can be measured with electroencephalography (EEG) using electrodes placed on the scalp.
研究者认为，可以把脑活动模式与脑电活动的变化相联系；后者可用放置于头皮上的电极，通过脑电图来测量。
Small EEG machines are already available, especially for computer gamers, which fit on the head.
小型头戴式脑电设备已经面世，有些特别为电脑游戏玩家设计。
paragraphs.gist: 表情识别有望读出顾客的微笑或皱眉，研究者也在探索用轻便的头戴式脑电设备取得与大型脑扫描仪相近的信息。

paragraphs.brief: 远程读取商品的隐私风险
sentences: The notion of shoppers wearing brain-scanning hats would be ridiculous if it were not so alarming.
买家戴脑部扫描帽子的观念如果不是那么令人惊恐的话将会是荒谬的
Privacy groups are already concerned about the rise of electronic surveillance that records what people do, let alone what they might be thinking.
隐私团体已经对电子监控的兴起感到担忧电子监控记录了人们的作为更不用说他们的想法了

The San Francisco-based Electronic Frontier Foundation is concerned that because RFID tags can be read at a distance by anyone with the necessary equipment they could create “privacy pollution”; being used to discover what is in not only someone’s shopping trolley but also their cupboards.
旧金山的电子前沿基金会担心，只要有设备，任何人都能远距离读取射频标签，这可能导致「隐私污染」：别人不仅能知道购物车里有什么，甚至能知道家中橱柜里放着什么。
paragraphs.gist: 隐私团体担心电子监控会从记录行为延伸到揣测想法，而且射频标签可远读，旁人甚至可能探知顾客家中橱柜里放了什么。

paragraphs.brief: 便利与折扣换取知情参与
sentences: To some degree shoppers would have to “buy in” to the process: a bit like having an account with an online retailer which comes with the explicit knowledge that your past purchases and browsing history will be monitored and used to pitch purchase suggestions.
在一定程度上，顾客得同意参与这一过程；这类似于在网店建立账户，清楚自己过去的购买和浏览记录会被追踪，用于推送购物建议。
And if that makes shopping easier—especially if sweetened with discounts—then consumers might sign up to it.
如果这样购物更方便，尤其是再给些折扣，消费者也许愿意参与。
When Dr Sharma asks shoppers what they think about his video-monitoring he says most people do not mind.
夏尔玛博士说，当他征询顾客对录像分析的意见时，大多数人并不介意。
paragraphs.gist: 如同同意网店根据浏览记录推荐商品，顾客若知情并能换来便利或折扣，可能愿意接受追踪；多数受访者也不介意摄像分析。

paragraphs.brief: 暗中操纵可能激怒顾客
sentences: But what if psychological selling is done stealthily?
但是如果心理销售是秘密进行的呢？
That way lies grave perils.
那样会很危险
It is the anger not of privacy groups that retailers should fear, but of customers at being manipulated from behind the scenes.
真正令零售商该担心的，是顾客发现自己被暗中操纵后的愤怒，而不只是隐私团体的不满。
paragraphs.gist: 商家若暗中使用心理手段，最大的风险是被顾客察觉自己受了操纵，进而引发他们本人的愤怒。

paragraphs.brief: 心理推销的限度与反弹
sentences: There have been backlashes before: “The Hidden Persuaders” by Vance Packard, an American journalist, caused a sensation when it was first published in 1957 by revealing psychological techniques used by advertisers, including subliminal messages.
类似的抵制以前也出现过。美国记者万斯·帕卡德的《暗藏的说服者》于 1957 年初版，书中揭露广告商利用包括潜意识信息在内的心理技巧，当时引起轰动。
It is what got Dr Spangenberg interested in the subject.
正是这本书引发了斯潘根伯格博士对这一课题的兴趣。
He thinks shopping science has limits.
他认为购物科学是有限度的
“I don’t think you are going to be able to make someone buy a car or a computer that they don’t need,” he says.
他说：“我不认为你会能够让某人买一辆车或电脑他们不需要。”
“But you might persuade them to choose one model instead of another.
「但你也许能让他们选这种型号，而不是另一种。
And importantly, they wouldn’t know it.”
更重要的是，他们不会知道这一点。
But if they did realise psychological methods were being used to influence their choice, “the counteraction can be so huge it can put someone off buying anything at all,” he adds.
但要是他们意识到自己的选择正受心理手段影响，他补充说：「反弹可能大到令他们什么都不愿买。」
paragraphs.gist: 心理推销或许能左右顾客选择哪个型号，却难以让人购买不需要的大件；一旦顾客意识到自己被操纵，甚至可能彻底放弃购买。

paragraphs.brief: 结账处最后一轮诱惑
sentences: Which is probably why at the end of this shopping trip there is not much in the trolley.
这或许正是这趟逛完之后购物车里没多少东西的原因。
At least the temptations at the checkout are easy to avoid: a few celebrity magazines and bags of sweets at the eye-level of children.
至少收银台边的诱惑还容易避开：无非是几本明星杂志，以及堆在儿童视线高度的一袋袋糖果。
But that will change too.
但是，这也将会改变。
paragraphs.gist: 作者购物结束时车里东西不多，眼下结账处的明星杂志和放在儿童视线高度的糖果尚易避开，但这些促销方式也在变化。

paragraphs.brief: 结账屏幕提供个性化广告
sentences: Barry Salzman, the chief executive of YCD Multimedia in New York, has big plans for the area around a cash till.
纽约 YCD Multimedia 的负责人巴里·萨尔兹曼对收银台周边区域有一番大计划。

He is using digital video screens displaying ads that relate to what someone is buying and which can also be linked with facial-recognition software to refine the displays according to the customer’s age or sex.
他使用数字视频屏幕显示与某人购买的东西有关的广告，这些广告也可以与面部识别软件挂钩，以便根据客户的年龄或性别改进显示。
His system is already being used in Aroma Espresso Bars in America to present, say, an advert for a chocolate croissant to someone buying only a cappuccino.
美国的 Aroma Espresso 咖啡店已在用这套系统，例如向只买一杯卡布奇诺的人展示巧克力可颂的广告。
paragraphs.gist: 数字屏可根据结账商品乃至顾客的年龄和性别调整广告，例如在咖啡店向只点了卡布奇诺的人推荐巧克力可颂。

paragraphs.brief: 未能结账的啤酒显出执行落差
sentences: But the checkout in this Sainsbury’s comes to a halt because the teenager at the till is not old enough to sell alcohol and can’t attract the attention of a supervisor for permission to ring up a multi-pack of beer, which is therefore left behind on the counter.
但这家森宝利的收银台却停了下来：值班的少年还没到可以售酒的年龄，也没能引起主管注意、取得为整组啤酒结账的许可，那组啤酒只好留在柜台上。
The science of shopping is a marvellously sophisticated business; the practice is still a little more primitive.
购物科学已经精妙至极，店里实际运行起来却还颇为原始。
paragraphs.gist: 一名未达售酒年龄的收银员找不到主管批准，一组啤酒只好留在柜台上；这次实际结账的小插曲映出了购物科学与店内运行的距离。

points: 超市借货架位置、商品选择和顾客行为数据影响购买。文章一边展示这些技术，一边追问它们的实际效果和隐蔽劝购的界线。
走进超市看布局 → 观察选择发生的瞬间 → 选项过多妨碍购买 → 隐蔽影响与现实限制
clauses: …, a friendly welcome is said to cut shoplifting.
连接词 whether 引出“Whether or not they boost sales”，说明主句的选择关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 whether 把这一层关系补进去。
Then there is the in-store bakery, ….
“which can be smelt before it is seen”修饰前面的 bakery。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 bakery，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Retailers are making breakthroughs in understanding their customers’ minds.
零售商对顾客购物心理的认识正在取得突破。
Here is what they know about you.
他们已经摸清了你购物时的哪些习惯？
